From records: degen is named as the iOS repo (this item; ruling ios-27-2-duo); ios-adblock is named by its repo name only, and no record I read says it ships an app, so unknown. Neither a nor b is picked, so the item stays open; nothing waits on it and main's rules stand until you say. Both options are about your own Nov 12 words, so only you or the consultant (who speaks for you) can rule here.
Goal: you only rule on what needs your word.
Problem (rule): Two of your Nov 12 rulings say one thing and main's rules say another. For each, one side has to give.
(1) The merge lock. You said: a Mac uses GitLock. Main says: GitLock only in the cloud; anywhere else uses GhLock.
(2) The simulator drive. You said: a drive takes a lease (a booking so two sessions never share one phone simulator). Main says: a drive that reuses a simulator already booted takes no lease.
What I found: the iOS repo degen follows main on (2), though one line of the iOS skill reads the other way. No repo shows a real case where the two versions gave different answers.
Based on (read): the retrospective's audit of 33 rulings; runner 11's read of degen.
Departs from: main — a keeps main as it is and rewrites your two Nov 12 rulings to match; b changes main to match your words.
Meanwhile: main's rules stand. Nothing waits on this.
